text: There were three little pigs. (Literally: "three little animals that say 'oink-oink'.") Each of them wanted to build a house. The first pig built a house of straw (literally: "little yellow plants") and finished very quickly. The second built his of sticks, also quickly. The third built his of stones (literally: "hard things"). It took him a long time. A wolf came and said: "Open the door! Let me in!" The pig said: "I won't!" The wolf blew hard (literally: "moved the air with his mouth"), and the straw house flew away! The first pig ran to the stick house. The wolf blew again, and the stick house flew away too! The two pigs ran to the stone house. The wolf blew and blew, but the stone house didn't move. He climbed in through the hole at the top (the chimney), but below there was hot water! The wolf got scared, rushed out, and never came back.

blind.whole: Three little animals called "heng-heng" each make a home. The first makes its home out of small gold-colored plants, which most likely means dry grass or straw. The second uses long things, probably sticks or wood. Both finish quickly. The third uses hard things, probably stones or bricks, and takes a long time. A big bad animal called "ao-ao" comes and tells them to open the door and let it in. A little animal refuses. The big bad animal blows hard and the plant home flies away, so the first little animal runs to the home of long things. That home is blown away too, so the two run to the home of hard things. The big bad animal blows and blows, but the hard home does not move. It climbs up and goes in through an opening at the top, but there is hot water below. It gets scared, gets out fast, and never comes back.
blind.unsure: S1: "heng-heng" is a sound word in quotes. It could be what each animal is named, or a name for the kind of animal taken from the sound it makes, like a grunt. The text does not say what kind of animal it is. S9: in the same way, "ao-ao" sounds like a howl, which could stand for the kind of animal or be its name. S3: the gloss gives jin as "money". I read it as gold, so the plants are gold-colored or yellow, which suggests dry grass or straw, but the text does not say so. S5 and S7: "long things" and "hard things" are vague. They could be sticks or wood and stones or bricks, but nothing narrows them down. S8: word for word it says "did a lot of time". I read it as spending a long time making the home. S11: which little animal speaks is not said. The "I" is singular, but it could stand for all of them. S12, S15, S18: "send out air with strength" I read as blowing hard, maybe at the house. The text does not say what it blows at. S13 and S16: "the home flies" I read as the home being blown away. It could also mean it flies apart. S20 and S21: "goes up" probably means climbing onto the roof, and "the opening at the top" could be a chimney or just a hole in the roof. S22: the hot water is below the opening, but the text does not say who put it there or what it is in. S23: "goes out" could mean it runs off out of the house, or it climbs back out the way it came in.

notes: Translated by hand following the translate skill (2026-10-22), at the level of the whole dictionary. For the author: kb_memory returns the book's own story-2 Hao-shuo-de (the story lines are in its pool, lesson none), so the test answer leaks; I reused those lines as the brief allows and named each change in its sentence's source. Grammar that would not read as meant: "Xiǎo dòng-wù kuài zǒu dào cháng dōng-xi-de jiā." never reads as ran to the house (dào is taken as a verb with cháng as its result), and "Liǎng-ge xiǎo dòng-wù kuài qù yìng dōng-xi-de jiā." reads only with qù + result yìng; adding le after qù fixes both. "Dà huài dòng-wù fā-chū kōng-qì, (yòu) fā-chū kōng-qì." reads only as a call (calling-hail) in all 500 readings, so the wolf is tā there. A dà huài dòng-wù subject reads first as dà + huài (verb) + dòng-wù, so the meant reading sits at numbers 17 to 186. "Tā hòu-lái ..." reads first as his later-part, so hòu-lái comes first. "Kāi mén! Ràng wǒ jìn-qù!" counts as two sentences for the checker, so it is joined with a comma. Glossary proposal: pig -> jiào "hēng-hēng"-de dòng-wù: the dictionary's dog and cat forms have this shape, and the 猪 form is 11 words. Glossary proposal: wolf (in a story) -> jiào "ào-ào"-de dà huài dòng-wù, then dà huài dòng-wù: short and the 狼 form's own sound. Glossary proposal: blow -> fā-chū kōng-qì, hard -> yòng lì fā-chū kōng-qì: the gloss form of 吹. Glossary proposal: straw -> jīn-de yánsè-de xiǎo zhíwù: the book's own phrase, no entry. Glossary proposal: chimney -> shàng-miàn-de kǒu: no entry. Glossary proposal: never came back -> hòu-lái ... méi huí-lái guò: méi ... guò is the form of 不曾. Glossary proposal: ran to a place -> kuài qù le X: kuài zǒu dào does not read as meant. Translated before kb_memory hid the stories' own lines (HAOSHUODE_MEMORY_SKIP), so some sentences reuse the book's lines and the book overlap is higher than a fresh run would give.
